chapter: On the road with Victor Spencer
title: Road trips and the Victor Spencer Cotton Club band
summary: He recalls gigs through Louisiana and Texas and the Victor Spencer band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah. Outside of the times when we was on the road, you know, going different places. Did you go on the road a lot? Oh yeah, when you see them bands, we used to give them gigs all through Louisiana, Texas, and different places like that. You know. And I was out there with Ike Garnett, with a group in Crowley, they're called the Yelping Hounds, I was out there with a group out there, and Victor De Spencer at the Shadowland, Victor De Spencer got the Shadowland. Well he had a band, he had a band too, with old man John Porter playing and Blake playing drums and Bunk was on trumpet and a boy by the name of, from St. Martinville, no he was from Lafayette, Edgar Mouton, he was playing sax, or you know Bunk was playing trumpet, you remember Bunk? And this guy, Hampton, playing trombone. Must have been years ago. Yeah, well I mean, and we had Tank Baptiste playing piano. Yeah. You see, but I was a youngster playing with older men than I was. And we had a council from Brobridge who used to play, he was automobile mechanic, played saxophone. You see, that was the New Orleans Cotton Club band, the Krells used to call it the New Orleans Coddy Pequon, you understand, and old man, and we had Al Agretta playing piano with us. Yeah, you heard of him, Al Agretta, he's in California now teaching and something like that. He was a great piano player. We had a good band.
Was this the Yelping Hounds you're talking about?
No, this was Cotton Club, Victor Spencer. Victor Spencer.

No, he had this band. Yelping Hounds, see Crowley was our Louisiana, with the exception of the year, jump off, you know. You see when we were hitting Lake Charles and all them different places, we'd take it from Crowley all the way, the Orange and all them places.
